q3_neutral_counting.ruling: a bare species name counts ions summed over charge states, neutrals excluded
q3_neutral_counting.what_the_writer_saw: the stored text of the BASE species names oxygen_density and boron_density: 'Total number density of oxygen atoms and ions across all charge states, from neutral to fully stripped' and 'Elemental boron number density, summed over neutral atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+'. The writer copied them because they are its nearest accepted neighbours.
q3_neutral_counting.own_dd_source: volume_averaged_oxygen_density and volume_averaged_boron_density resolve to summary/volume_average/n_i/<species>, an ion density. Neutrals are not in their own source.
q3_neutral_counting.corrected_conclusion: CORRECTION to the first version of this record, which said these names' DD source includes neutral atoms. It does not. The source is an ion density; the neutral wording enters only through the stored text of the base names oxygen_density and boron_density, which contradict the ions-only ruling and are what the writer copied.
q3_neutral_counting.remedy: ordering, not a rename, which is the opposite of the first version's ruling. Rewrite the base species names oxygen_density and boron_density first, so the volume_averaged_* names derived from them copy an ions-only definition rather than an elemental-atom one. The base names are the defect; the derived names are downstream of it.
q3_neutral_counting.note_on_neutral_species_density: volume_averaged_neutral_species_density is excluded from the population rule by docs_gates.is_species_density_name (neutral_species is an aggregate subject), yet the bulk pass applied the species hint to it and drove three rotations against text that was already right for its name.

repairs.defect: generate_docs gives the model every settled shared part verbatim (shared_parts), but refine_docs built neither the context key nor a template block. The renderer still installs the stored sentence and the persistence gate refuses a paraphrase, so every rotation re-guesses wording it cannot land and spends a rotation until the escalation seat happens to reproduce it.
repairs.evidence: two names each burned three rotations and one escalation call; the escalation call is 57 percent of the five-name spend
repairs.test: tests/standard_names/test_refine_docs_worker_context.py drives process_refine_docs_batch's own context-building path and asserts on the context the worker hands the renderer. It fails against a tree built from a084551a5 (1 failed, EXIT=1) and passes at the head tree (1 passed, EXIT=0); it also fails when the shared_parts lines are reverted from the head tree. The earlier template tests built their own context, so they guarded the template but not the worker. The covering suite tests/standard_names/ was run as a SLURM all_debug job on the repaired tree: 8756 passed, 0 failed, EXIT=0 (job 1314959).
repairs.template_sharing: The settled-wording block is one partial, sn/_shared_parts.md, included by both generate_docs_user and refine_docs_user, so the two templates cannot drift. The block had been pasted into both.

q4_cheapest_correct_route.method: per class, the cheapest route is the one that reaches the acceptance score on its first generated draft, because a rotation costs one refine call plus a re-review and the third rotation costs the escalation seat

classes.route: one generate with the settled sentence in shared_parts, then one review; no refine
one generate plus refine only where the parent has more than one child shape; hold a parent that is only a grouping from the cut
one generate with the operator registry sentence in shared_parts, then one review
one generate plus one refine, since a unit mismatch is a definition rewrite, not a wording substitution
one generate plus one refine, the readers' phrase as the reason
not attemptable: waiting on the grammar release; zero spend
